ai.title: System instruction tags for tool results
ai.summary: Added system instruction tags to clarify tool results are not user messages. Updated main-prompt.ts, agent-instructions.md, tools.ts.

eli5.text: The AI assistant now has clearer instructions to understand that messages wrapped in special tags are coming from the system itself (like tool results), not from you directly. This helps prevent confusion where the assistant might mistakenly think the system is asking for permission or giving commands on your behalf. If you looked closely, you'd see that when tools run, their outputs are now explicitly labeled as system-only messages, and the assistant is told not to interpret these as user questions or approvals. The change is live today for anyone using the assistant.

ai.title: Track agentstep event in main prompt
ai.summary: Added `AGENT_STEP` event tracking in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and defined the corresponding enum value `backend.agent_step` in `common/src/constants/analytics-events.ts`. The new event captures `agentStepId`, `clientSessionId`, `fingerprintId`, `userInputId`, and `userId` at the start of each agent loop step. This enables correlation of logs and analytics within a single agent execution cycle.

eli5.text: Every time the assistant takes a step while working through your request, the system now quietly logs a marker that links that single step to you, your session, and the specific input prompt. If you glance at the backend logs, you would see each agent step tied together by a shared identifier instead of floating as separate entries. You would not notice any visible change in how the assistant responds, but the behind-the-scenes tracking is now live and actively recording these events.

ai.title: Reduce agentic behavior in lite mode
ai.summary: Adds `isLiteMode` check to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to conditionally disable verification steps and strict completion mandates when `costMode` is 'lite'. Lite mode now omits instructions to run type checkers/linters, close tags, or complete all steps before ending turn. This reduces token usage and latency for low-cost interactions.

eli5.text: When you talk to the assistant in a cheaper, faster mode, it now skips extra housekeeping steps. Instead of running checks, tests, and linters after each change, the assistant focuses on your request only, then ends its turn. You'll get a quicker back-and-forth at the cost of less strict code verification. This live today: lite mode interactions are less thorough but faster, while default mode keeps its pre-finish quality checks.

ai.title: Reduce logger chunk limit to 65535
ai.summary: Changed `MAX_LENGTH` constant in `backend/src/util/logger.ts` from 70,000 to 65,535. This aligns the log chunk size with potential 65,535 byte limits observed in some environments, replacing the previous buffer assumption for 100k total size. Affects backend logging utility only.

eli5.text: Internal logging tools now break up log entries into smaller chunks of roughly 65,535 characters instead of the previous 70,000. This tweak helps avoid potential size limits that some environments enforce on individual log chunks. The change only affects how logs are stored internally and does not affect any user-facing features.

constants.name: MAX_LENGTH
constants.from: 70_000 // Max total log size is 100k, put some buffer
constants.to: 65535 // Max total log size is sometimes 100k (sometimes 65535?)

ai.title: Improve warnings for invalid XML in stream parser
ai.summary: backend/src/xml-stream-parser.ts adds WARN prefix and actionable guidance to onError calls for malformed tool XML. Covers unclosed tools/params, stray tags, duplicate params, and end-of-stream auto-closure. Affects backend XML stream processing.

eli5.text: When the assistant receives a malformed tool call (for example, one with an unclosed parameter or a stray tag), it now emits a clearly prefixed warning that tells you exactly what to fix. If you look at the logs while it processes a stream, you will see messages starting with WARN followed by actionable guidance instead of the previous terse descriptions. This is live today for any backend process that consumes the stream parser.

ai.title: Clarify user vs assistant cwd in prompts and terminal output
ai.summary: System prompt and terminal output now explicitly distinguish between user cwd and assistant cwd. `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` injects `**user** cwd` with a note that assistant cwd is project root. `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` appends the same clarification to the final cwd status message.

eli5.text: When you ask for help from the AI assistant, it now clearly says which folder you are currently in (your "user cwd") and reminds you that the assistant itself works from the project's main folder. You'll see this note both in the instructions the assistant receives and in the terminal message that shows your final folder at the end of a session. This stops any mix-up about where files are being read from or saved to.

ai.title: Fix types in display.ts
ai.summary: Update `process.stdout.write` and `process.stderr.write` signatures in `npm-app/src/display.ts`. Change callback error type from `Error | undefined` to `Error | null | undefined` to match Node.js types. Fixes GitHub Actions type check failure.

eli5.text: A small behind-the-scenes adjustment was made to the program's internal logging system, correcting a type mismatch that was causing automated checks to fail. This only affects the development process, not the program's visible behavior. If you looked at the running program, you would notice nothing different.

ai.title: CI workflow adds system info step
ai.summary: Added Print System Info step to .github/workflows/ci.yml logging process.arch and process.platform via bun. Aids GitHub Actions diagnosis. Internal CI only.

eli5.text: The automated testing system now prints out what kind of computer it's running on so engineers can better figure out what's going on when something breaks. This shows up as extra output in the system logs when the software checks itself behind the scenes, but you won't see any direct change to how your programs run.

ai.title: CI Bun 1.2.12 and tree-sitter debug
ai.summary: CI workflow `.github/workflows/ci.yml` upgrades `oven-sh/setup-bun` version from 1.1.26 to 1.2.12. Added `ls` commands in the 'Print System Info' step to inspect `tree-sitter/prebuilds` directories. Scope limited to CI pipeline configuration.

eli5.text: The automated system that checks whether new code works correctly has been updated to use a newer version of its tooling, which helps it run faster and more reliably. While it runs, you can see it now glances at a couple of directories related to a code-parsing library to help catch problems before they slip through. This only affects the behind-the-scenes checks, not any app or feature you interact with day to day.

ai.title: Move tree-sitter debug commands to build step
ai.summary: Removed dedicated Print System Info step. Moved architecture, platform, and prebuild directory checks into Build and typecheck. Ensures debug output appears after bun run build executes.

eli5.text: The system's behind-the-scenes setup process now checks what kind of environment it's running in (like whether it's Mac or Windows, and what processor it has) at the very end of the setup, right after it finishes building everything. Previously, these checks happened at a separate early step; now they're grouped with the final build verification so you only see them once everything else is ready. If you watch the setup logs, you'll notice these environment details appear alongside the final build success message instead of near the beginning.

ai.title: Fix out of order chunks in Saxy XML parser
ai.summary: Saxy replaces `_entityBuffer` with `_wait(Node.text, ...)` for incomplete entities. Ensures chunks parse in correct order. Scope: `common/src/util/saxy.ts`.

eli5.text: If you send chunks of XML text to the assistant in separate pieces, the parser sometimes glued them together in the wrong order, which could drop or scramble part of the data. The fix makes it wait and hold an incomplete piece until the rest arrives, then processes them in the correct sequence, so partial text arrives intact. You’d notice by receiving complete text instead of fragments that previously went missing or arrived garbled.

ai.title: ci.yml fix stray quote tree-sitter prebuilds ls
ai.summary: Removed stray single quote in `ls node_modules/tree-sitter/prebuilds/linux-x64` command within `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Syntax error broke CI job execution. Scope limited to CI configuration.

eli5.text: When the project's automated testing system ran, it tried to look at a folder called tree-sitter/prebuilds/linux-x64, but a stray single quote in the command made the system choke and stop the test run before it could finish checking the rest of the project. That one-character typo broke the entire batch of automated checks that developers rely on to catch problems before merging code changes. Removing the stray quote lets the command run properly again, so the testing automation will move through its steps without tripping over a syntax error. If you were watching the test logs, you'd see the run failing right at that folder listing step and then stopping instead of continuing to the type checks.

ai.title: Add debug logging to tool-renderers unit test
ai.summary: Added a try-catch block around the `require('../tool-renderers')` call in `npm-app/src/utils/__tests__/tool-renderers.test.ts`. The catch block logs the error object and the string 'asdf' to the console. This change is internal to the test suite and does not affect production code or user-facing behavior.

eli5.text: The test suite has added a small safety net that prints extra information whenever it fails to load the tool-renderers module during testing. Developers running tests will now see a console message containing the error details and a marker string if that loading step fails. This is a behind-the-scenes change to make debugging test failures easier, and it does not affect any functionality you use directly.

ai.title: Remove CI tree-sitter debugging logs
ai.summary: Removed temporary architecture and platform logging commands from the Build and typecheck step in ci.yml. These diagnostics were used to inspect tree-sitter prebuilds and are no longer required. The change also includes minor import formatting updates in packages/code-map/parse.ts.

eli5.text: The build system's diagnostic logging commands that were temporarily printing out architecture and platform details for tree-sitter prebuilds have been removed, so the build output is now cleaner during the Build and typecheck step. This affects only the internal continuous integration process that developers see when running builds, not any end-user experience, and you would notice fewer console.log statements in the CI workflow output if you watched a build run. A small formatting adjustment was also made to import statements in one file, but this has no functional impact. The change is live today as part of the latest code merge.

ai.title: CI: add tmate debug hook, reduce test retries
ai.summary: Added `mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3` step to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, triggered on `inputs.debug == 'true'` or `failure()`. Reduced `nick-fields/retry@v3` `max_attempts` from 5 to 1 for test execution. Scope: CI pipeline only.

eli5.text: When a software test fails during development, the system now opens a live debugging session that developers can join remotely to investigate the problem in real time. At the same time, automated tests no longer retry five times before giving up, they now try exactly once, so failures surface immediately instead of being masked by repeated attempts. This affects only the internal testing pipeline and does not change anything end users see or experience.

ai.title: CI debug shell gated to workflowdispatch with access limit
ai.summary: Interactive debug shell step in `ci.yml` now requires `workflow_dispatch` and `inputs.debug_enabled` or `failure()`. Replaced `inputs.debug == 'true'` check with `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.debug_enabled`. Added `limit-access-to-actor: true` to restrict tmate session access to the triggering user. Includes `timeout-minutes: 30` guard.

eli5.text: The automated system now only unlocks the live troubleshooting session when someone intentionally triggers it by hand and turns on the debug switch, or when a problem is detected automatically. Previously it could start more freely, but now it waits for an explicit go-ahead and keeps the session limited to 30 minutes. Only the person who started the work can join that live session, so unrelated people can't drop in. This change is live today in the internal workflow.

ai.title: CI: Reorder test run after debug shell, add tree-sitter prebuilds
ai.summary: Moved 'Run tests' step after 'Open interactive debug shell' in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Added diagnostic steps listing node_modules/tree-sitter/prebuilds/linux-x64 contents. This change likely aims to debug CI failures by allowing shell access before tests run, while checking tree-sitter binary availability.

eli5.text: When the team runs their automated checks on new code, they first open a temporary access point so a developer can connect and look around before the tests run, then they run the test suite. If a test fails, the developer can jump in early and investigate what files exist and whether a specific helper tool is properly installed, instead of only getting a message after everything breaks. This is live today for the team's internal verification process.

ai.title: Remove debug shell and ls commands from CI workflow
ai.summary: Removed `ls` commands and an interactive debug shell from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The `mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3` step was deleted entirely. This cleans up the CI logs and removes the manual intervention step for the test job.

eli5.text: The automated checks that run behind the scenes when code is proposed have been quietly cleaned up. The team removed a set of commands that were just listing files for debugging, and they took out a special manual-only debugging session that developers could open during a check. You won't see any difference in how the checks run now, but developers will see cleaner logs when something goes wrong.

ai.title: CI debug shell now triggers on failure
ai.summary: Interactive debug shell step in .github/workflows/ci.yml now runs conditionally via `if: failure()`. This restricts tmate session creation to failed jobs, preventing unnecessary shell spawns during successful test runs. Change affects CI pipeline behavior for all matrix packages.

eli5.text: When a test run succeeds, it no longer launches a live debugging session for you to connect to; the session now only starts if a test fails. So on green builds you just get the pass result, and on red builds you get the interactive shell automatically. This applies to the shared CI pipeline used across all tested packages, and the new step is live today.

ai.title: Reorder debug shell step in CI workflow
ai.summary: Moved the `mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3` step from before the test execution to after the `nick-fields/retry@v3` test step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The debug shell now triggers only after tests complete or fail, rather than interrupting the test run. This ensures the interactive debug session captures the state after test execution logic has finished.

eli5.text: When a test run breaks in the project's automated checking system, an interactive debugging session now pops open only after the tests have finished running or failed, instead of interrupting the test run itself. Previously, a developer trying to debug a failure could accidentally disrupt the tests still in progress; now the debugging session connects to a system that has already completed its test steps, so the developer sees the state right after the tests did their work. This only affects contributors working inside the project's internal continuous-testing setup, and the change is in effect today.

ai.title: Initialize balance breakdown with all grant types
ai.summary: The `calculateUsageAndBalance` function now initializes `breakdown` and `principals` objects with all `GrantTypeValues` set to 0, rather than starting with empty objects. This change ensures that the `CreditBalance` interface strictly requires a `Record<GrantType, number>` instead of a `Partial<Record<GrantType, number>>`, eliminating the need for optional chaining or defaulting logic in consumers like `usage-display.tsx`. The `GrantTypeValues` constant in `common/src/types/grant.ts` was updated to use `as const` to support this strict typing.

eli5.text: When you look at your account's credit page, you now always see a number under every kind of credit you might have earned (free credits, referral credits, purchased credits, and admin credits), filling in 0 where appropriate instead of just leaving those spots blank. Behind the scenes, the system now starts its calculations with all four credit types pre-filled with zero rather than building the list one by one, so it no longer has to guess what's missing later and display logic can skip the safety checks it used to need.

ai.title: Update Saxy XML parser tests to match current event emission behavior
ai.summary: Test suite updated to align with current Saxy parser behavior where tag events now include `rawTag` data. Assertions reflect changes in whitespace handling and immediate text emission for entities. The parser now emits `tagclose` events for invalid closing tags instead of treating them as text. Covers `common/src/util/__tests__/saxy.test.ts`.

eli5.text: The system fixed its XML-reading tests so they match how the parser actually behaves now: tag events carry extra detail (like the raw text of the tag), whitespace is handled differently, and malformed closing tags are reported as errors instead of being treated as regular text. This is behind-the-scenes test maintenance and does not change anything you see; the parser itself was already emitting this behavior, and only the test expectations were updated to stay accurate.

ai.title: CI test discovery uses find instead of glob
ai.summary: CI matrix `test_path` renamed `test_paths` and replaced static globs with `$(find <src> -name '*.test.ts')` for npm-app, backend, common. Fixes glob syntax mismatch where `**` in single quotes failed recursive matching in shell. Affects `.github/workflows/ci.yml` only.

eli5.text: The automated test system that runs on every code change now finds test files by searching the project folders directly, instead of listing them with a pattern that was missing some files. Only the internal test configuration was updated; nothing in the app you use looks different. If you opened the GitHub workflow file, you would see the test list entries renamed from one line each to a single search command. This is live today and only affects how the company's internal tests are gathered.

ai.title: Bump Bun to 1.2.12 in CI
ai.summary: CI workflow `bun-version` updated from 1.1.26 to 1.2.12 in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Aligns CI environment with current Bun stable release. Affects all CI jobs using `oven-sh/setup-bun`.

eli5.text: Nothing for you to notice, this is behind-the-scenes maintenance. The team updated the version of a JavaScript runtime used only during automated testing of their code, keeping it current with the latest stable release. This change affects only the internal testing environment, not anything you see or use.

ai.title: Fix balance calculation to always itemize principals
ai.summary: Balance calculation now itemizes grant principals for all active grants, regardless of balance status. Previously, principals were only added to the breakdown if the grant balance was positive, causing underreporting for zero or negative balance grants. This change affects packages/billing/src/balance-calculator.ts. The fix moves the principal addition outside the balance check, ensuring accurate accounting for all active grants.

eli5.text: When the system totals up how much money a provider has given you across your active grants, it now always includes the principal amount granted for every active grant, even when a grant's running balance is zero or below. Before, the principal was only added when a grant still had a positive balance remaining, so the breakdown could leave out principal contributions you had already used up or that had gone negative. If you look at your balance summary today, the itemized principal totals will now match every grant you currently hold, and you will not see the principal line disappear just because a grant balance dipped to zero or below.

eli5.text: The automated system that checks the codebase was finding the wrong files to test, so some tests were being skipped. Now it looks up the correct test files right when it runs, instead of guessing them ahead of time. If you saw the check results, you'd notice more test files being picked up. The fix is live in the project's internal checking system.

ai.title: Comment out action-tmate in CI
ai.summary: Disables the interactive debug shell step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` by commenting out `mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3`. This prevents the workflow from opening a tmate session on failure, which was previously configured with a 15-minute timeout guard. The change is internal to the CI configuration and does not affect user-facing functionality.

eli5.text: When the project's automated tests fail, the system used to open a temporary remote terminal so developers could poke around and figure out what went wrong, but it would only stay open for up to 15 minutes. The settings that turned on that debug terminal have now been switched off, so a failing test run will no longer launch that interactive session. You won't see this change yourself unless you were a developer relying on that debug shell when troubleshooting a broken build.
